_patch_meta.description: Supersede the Programme sections 10 and 55 so that step 3.3 reads as the researcher ruled on 2026-11-25: one new observation for each unique match across the observations that reference more than one collection (#2538).

record.body:
The programme organises its work into three stages: **Base_data**, **Analysis** and **Publishing**. Each stage has its own live mechanism, governed by its own configuration. The database carries each stage's state, and work is taken up at the point the database shows it left off.

**Base_data** runs from the text of the Bible to the identification of the surfaces. It has three parts, each built on the one before.

*The text and its data.* Every verse of the Bible is taken from STEP Bible together with its Hebrew and Greek words, their Strong's identities, meanings and relations, and the verse's interlinear presentation is kept verbatim. The mechanical reading of each verse (`verse_lexical`) is derived once from it and records the verse's structural composition and nothing of what a word does for the inner being. This is built verse by verse, by book and range, before any collection exists, and it is complete before any collection is read. Collections play no part in how it is batched.

*The surfaces.* The English words and phrases of the ESV, each linked through its Strong's codes to the original words behind it, are the population the study draws on. The whole population is sorted, by deduction and likeness, into four surface groups: behaviour, inner_being_state, entity and other. The sorting is roughly nine in ten correct, by the researcher's assessment, within an accepted margin; the items placed wrongly are found in the deeper analysis and compensated for there. Its purpose is to make the reading of the inner being's working possible.

*The collections.* The surfaces of the first two groups are collated, by the likeness or relatedness of the behaviour they name, into collections. Each surface belongs to one collection, and through the Strong's code of its base it is connected with its verses, so that a collection carries the verses its surfaces occur in (Chapter 4).

*The engagement step.* A surface is sorted into its group by what it names, before its verses are read, and what it does in a verse is settled only by reading the verse. The engagement step, run on a collection before the collection is read, assesses each member surface in each verse it occurs in, by the role it takes there, and the surface's group then follows from the roles. A surface that is a characteristic in any of its verses is a behaviour, and the difference between its verses is carried by the observations of each verse and not by the group. A surface that is a characteristic in none but is a qualifier in some is an inner-being state. A surface with no inner-being role in any verse leaves the study group, and each such departure is raised as a question for the researcher. A surface judged to have no bearing in a verse is recorded as a silence with the role standalone, and those verses are reviewed again, so that a surface found on re-reading to have a significant role in conjunction with another surface is given that role. Everything the step assesses is inferential until the researcher confirms it. The roles are set out in Chapter 4, under the node.

**Analysis** reads the inner being's working from the verses of the collections. The objective is to read those verses and deduce from them how the inner being works. A whole collection cannot be read in one go: to understand both the lexical context of the words in a verse and the inner-being working of the many behaviours a verse or group of verses carries is not achievable in one pass. The work is therefore split into units, and the units are read in layers and in stages.

*The unit.* To make a collection digestible, its surfaces are grouped further into surface subgroups. The subgroup is the unit of reading. In this programme "surface group" means one of the four groups of the surfaces, and a group of the surfaces of one collection is a subgroup.

*The layers.* Each layer deposits its findings as observations, so that they are available to the next layer, and each collection is digested into observations of lexical meaning first and of the inner-being working afterwards. The work of one collection runs in this order. First the grouping: every surface of the collection is allocated to a subgroup, from the WordNet tables and by meaning in context, reading no verse; every surface, through its Strong's codes, has its verses. Then, for one subgroup at a time and in isolation, one set of data is pulled once (the subgroup's surfaces, every verse they stand in with the full verse text and the full verse-lexical, the existing observations in scope, and the WordNet pairings) and every step of the loop works on it. The loop makes the evidence observations first: the word step writes one observation for each distinct finding about a surface, with a node for each occurrence it holds in (the same surface in several verses is several nodes of one observation); the sense step gathers those readings into the senses of the subgroup and writes one observation for each sense, traced back to the word observations by traced nodes; the pairing step (step 2.1) writes one observation for each distinct finding of an item, with a node for each verse it holds in, built on the sense observations and sometimes the word observations, again traced. The sweep then judges what is left of the old observations, and the evidence validation closes the evidence layer for the subgroup. Only then does the inner-being layer start: step 3.1 builds the inner-being observations of the subgroup from its evidence, resting on the sense observations first. The lexical layers and the inner-being layer are separate processes and never run together, a step closes before the next opens, and every aspect a step demands is answered by an observation with its nodes, or by a recorded none with its reason. The steps the configuration holds, with what each asks, reads and leaves, are set out in Chapter 6, in the section 'The collection reading'; the rules that govern the observation and the node are in the configuration, and the section on the node in Chapter 4 describes how a node ties an observation to the text.

*The stages.* The researcher's stages, set on 2026-11-15, are five. The table gives, for each, what it is, the unit it works on and where it stands. The order of the work is not the order of the numbers: the grouping (stage 2) comes first, and the word step (stage 1) is then the first step inside each subgroup.

| Stage | What it is | The unit | Where it stands |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Lexical analysis of the words | What each word is and how it is used in each verse it stands in, read from the verse, the stored structure and the lexicon entries of its Strong's code. Lexical only; it says nothing of the inner being. | The surface with its Strong's code: one observation for each distinct finding about it, with a node for each occurrence it holds in. | Specified 2026-11-25; the code is being aligned. |
| 2. Grouping of the surfaces | The four surface groups, the collections, and the subgroups within a collection. A subgroup is made from the WordNet tables (surfaces joined by a same-base or both pair are one seed group; a surface WordNet does not hold is a subgroup of its own) and by meaning in context; no verse is read. The surface is placed whole in one subgroup, and its Strong's codes are evidence of its different senses. The subgroups are indicative of words that may relate to each other and differentiate or accentuate senses; they state nothing of the inner being. | The surface within its collection: placed in a subgroup, or set aside with its reason. | The surface groups and the collections are made. The grouping tools are built; thought's seven subgroups were made by the earlier verse-reading method and are made again by this one. |
| 3. Verse-lexical observations | For each subgroup: its senses (steps 1.1 and 1.2: one observation for each sense and one for the Strong's enrichment of each sense, each traced to the word observations), and what stands with it in the verses (step 2.1: pairings, qualifiers, entities, direction, a double meaning; one observation for each distinct finding, with a node for each verse it holds in, traced to the senses and sometimes the word observations). A sense is driven by meaning in context, from the Strong's code, the lexicon and the verse, not from the English surface alone; one surface can carry several senses and several surfaces one. Lexical only. | The subgroup, and within it the sense and the verse. | Specified 2026-11-25; the code writes one observation for the whole subgroup with no traces and is being aligned. |
| 4. Inner-being analysis | The inner-being observations, built from the evidence observations (the senses first, because the workings of the inner being work with senses more than with individual surfaces). Step 3.1 is made for each subgroup as the last step of its loop; step 3.2 gathers the behaviours of the collection from all its subgroups; step 3.3 reads all the observations whose nodes reference more than one collection and records one new observation for each unique match across them (the basis for a deeper analysis of what each pairing means; there is no minimum, no cap and no judgement of significance, and the volume is not yet known), and opens only when the nodes of the observations it reads carry the collection on both sides and the partner collections are complete (the collection status is checked, then the researcher is asked). The inner-being validation completes after step 3.3. It formulates no claim. | The subgroup (3.1), the collection (3.2), the collections (3.3). | Specified and built in outline (2026-11-21, #2528); respecified 2026-11-25; it has not been run on any collection. |
| 5. Claims | Pulls the stage 4 observations together into behaviour statements, and updates the claims register. It discovers no building block (that is stage 4), and the surface groups fall away in it: stage 5 receives observations only. | The observations. | Not decided. |

The order of the layers is now settled. The grouping is made first, from the WordNet tables, and the word step then reads inside each subgroup, because a surface is placed whole in one subgroup and its words are read inside it; the stage numbers are kept as names and no longer as the order of work.

*What the subgroup is for.* The researcher's reasoning, recorded when the layered reading was defined, is this. A collection holds words that carry one concept in many forms, and its subgroups are the concepts inside it: surfaces of like meaning, such as the derivatives of one word that travel together. A subgroup is not itself a sense: it is indicative of words that may relate to each other and may differentiate or accentuate senses, and the senses are found inside it by meaning in context. Gathering the surfaces lets a finding be stated once for a sense and not once for each surface, while the verses of every surface travel with it through the nodes, so that an observation made for the subgroup is found for each of its verses. In stage 3 the subgroup is the unit every observation is keyed to: its senses, their enrichment from the Strong's codes, which links each to its usage in the verses, and then what stands with it in the verses, the qualifiers, the entities and the direction the text states. Reading the subgroup also tests the grouping: where a grouping is found wrong it is reformed. In stage 4 the same subgroups carry the inner-being observations. A word is not analysed alone in the claims reading; it is bound with its partner, the characteristic, or it is excluded, and a word wrongly included in a collection is moved to entity or other and the move is processed, so that the completeness tests continue to hold. The lexical layers prepare the base data for the formulation of claims.

*Volume.* The collection is the unit of a sitting of the tools, and the subgroup is the unit of the loop: the data of one subgroup is pulled once and every step of its loop works on it, and nothing of another subgroup is read. Every read is by an indexed lookup in chunks and never a pass over a large table. The word step is the largest part of the work; the same surface in several verses is several nodes of one observation, not several observations. The pull limits nothing that the reading needs. The filled file is checked as a whole and written in one transaction, and a problem anywhere in it refuses the whole file. A row stays open until it is recorded and validated, so a collection can be left partly answered and the next pull returns what is left. The configuration sets no order in which the collections are taken and no number of rows for one sitting; the order is decided with its reason stated, and the researcher may overrule. A job that runs longer than a few minutes is started outside the working session, with a log, so that it can be checked, stopped and resumed.

*Gates.* A step closes only when every row it demands is answered by an observation with its nodes, or by a recorded none with its reason, and validated by the check; the next step does not open before it. The steps of the loop do not open until the grouping of the collection is finished: every surface placed or set aside with its reason, and every subgroup holding a surface. The loop is for one subgroup at a time. Step 3.1 of a subgroup opens when the evidence validation of that subgroup passes; it does not wait for the other subgroups. Step 3.2 opens when every subgroup's step 3.1 is closed. Step 3.3 opens only when the nodes of the observations carry the collection on both sides and no partner collection in the observations is incomplete; the collection status is checked first and the researcher is asked. The inner-being validation starts after the loop and completes after step 3.3. A stage that finds an earlier observation wrong does not correct it in place: the case returns to the earlier stage, where a row answered again withdraws its earlier observation with its reason.

*What stage 3 leaves.* When stage 3 is complete a subgroup holds, for each of its surfaces, an observation for each distinct finding about it, with a node for each verse it holds in (the word step); for each sense, an observation of its meaning and an observation of its Strong's enrichment, each traced to the word observations it covers, every word observation being carried by exactly one sense; and, for each distinct finding, a pairing, a qualifier, an entity and the direction the text states, with a node for each verse it holds in, and a double meaning for each surface that carries two or more Strong's codes, each traced to the senses it builds on. There is no minimum number of shared verses. Each is an observation with its nodes, each node carrying its verse, word, surface, collection and subgroup, and the set is the complete verse-lexical account of the subgroup. Stage 4 reads that account. What each of these observations states is what the dictionary, the verses and the stored structure show: the grammatical qualifier is a stage 3 observation, and what the qualifier gives the behaviour in place is a stage 4 observation.

*Fallout.* Some surfaces, words and aspects are not analysed, and the programme states what is done about each.

| What is not analysed | What is done |
|---|---|
| Surfaces of the groups entity and other | They are not members of any collection. They enter the study as the words that stand with a collection's surfaces, as nodes of the observation that covers them. A verse that holds only such surfaces is out of scope and is not touched. |
| A word wrongly included in a collection | It is found at any stage and moved by the procedure for changing a collection, and the move is processed so that the step reopens. |
| Surfaces wrongly sorted into the four groups, unjudged or set aside | They are found in the deeper analysis and compensated for there; the step that records them is not yet defined. |
| A surface plainly not a member of the collection in meaning | It is set aside in the grouping with its reason and moved out by the procedure for changing a collection. |
| A function word | It is read with its unit and has no row of its own, except a negator and a connective. |
| A qualifier, an entity or a double meaning that is not present | A recorded none with its reason, where the step allows it. |
| An aspect of a Strong's code that the verses do not carry | It is not a conflict or an error; no observation need focus on a meaning that is not about the inner being. |
| Surfaces not yet placed in a subgroup | They stop stage 3 from opening for the collection until they are placed or set aside. |

*What the inner-being layer reads.* Stage 4 reads how the inner being works from the observations of stage 3. The researcher's placement is settled: how the inner being is read belongs to this layer, and what the readings show together, how workings are grained and linked, how states and transitions behave and how a characteristic emerges, belongs to the claims, where the answers are discovered from the observations. The order of the study is to finish reading the inner-being surface groups into observations and then to formulate the claims. The researcher has stated what is read: behaviour is not only acts or operations but also states and conditions, for example sin, righteousness, life and death; it has qualifiers that define it; and a characteristic such as anger or love is not a thing and is not defined in advance, being known only by inference from the collection of behaviours, processes, actions and movements that give it substance. The programme's record of how the working has been defined, from the first working definition to the layers, shows the same few parts recurring under different names: the bearer and the seat, the behaviour in its three forms of act, state and movement, the qualifiers, the source and the object, the effect, the link to other workings, the expression or what is hidden behind it, and the context of the passage. The lexical layers hold a home for few of these, and the inner-being layer needs one for the bearer, the state of a being, the transition, the effect, the expression, the context and the link. This is the record's reading and it is inferential until the researcher confirms it. The study has also defined the interventions that a reading triggers: read beyond the verse, in its passage, genre and speaker; read outward from the verse and not inward from a question; check the original; reclassify a word whose role in this verse is not the one its collection gives it; do not force a meaning and never close on 'not X'; record a discovery outside the verse separately. They are carried into the layered reading as the interventions that every stage 4 row prompts (cfg_setting layer.interventions). The test applied to every result is whether it is sensible, reasonable and defensible. The rules of this reading are already held in the configuration: nine items explored for every characteristic (meaning, role, polarity, object, enactment, party with its route, circumstance, operation with its chain, and a flag), eight kinds of finding, the node roles, the method rules of the reading step on how a verse is read and how a finding is written, and sixteen nuance pointers. Stage 4 is built from them: what stages 1 and 3 now do is taken out, the rest is placed on the collection, the subgroup and the ledger, and the level across subgroups and collections and the interventions listed above are added. Every finding of a stage 4 row rests on named observations and carries nodes with the role the reading gives each occurrence; an occurrence outside the observations it rests on is allowed only with a recorded read-back (the verse and the reason), and a word that holds nothing for the inner being takes the role standalone.

*Role in the inner-being layer.* The role a word has in a verse is what the inner-being layer reads by. It is judged for each occurrence, from the verse and against what the verse is about, and never taken from the cluster tag, from the collection or from the part the word usually plays: the same word can be a characteristic in one verse and a qualifier in another, and a word that has no inner-being role in a verse is not forced into one (the node, in Chapter 4, sets out the roles). Two consequences are the researcher's. The role is the filter of the deeper reading: the deeper reading of the verses in the next phase is filtered on the role of the words, so that the study is not contaminated by words that have little or no bearing on the inner being; where that filter sits in the claims phase is not yet defined, and it is not built. And a role is never a verdict: a verse or an item is never closed as 'only a qualifier' or 'no bearing'. What is recorded is what the verse is, with every significance it carries, since a verse often carries two or three and none is dropped because it was not the one asked about.

*The claims.* Claims are formulated from the inner-being observations. The formulation of claims is not yet decided. The claims that exist come from an earlier method and are not yet tied to the collections; each is to be cross-linked to its collection and re-evaluated against the observations.

**Publishing** is the production of the essays and output that carry the results: the narrative, held in the database as chapters and sections, and exported for its readers.

**Where the programme stands.** The base data is complete for the Bible: every verse, its original-language data and its mechanical reading. The surfaces are sorted into the four groups, with a small remainder not yet judged, and the surfaces of behaviour and inner_being_state are gathered into collections. The reading, which is the centre of the study, has not properly started. No collection has completed a stage, no subgroup has been made by the grouping method now specified, and no stage 3 observation of the current design exists. The specification of 2026-11-25 is the reference for the loop, and the code is being aligned to it. The observations in the database were made by earlier methods (documents captured, readings by cluster, by strand and by phase) and are held as gathered rows; every one that can be related to a collection and its verses is in scope for that collection, and the word step clears them: one is re-applied or corrected, or, if it is still unmarked and not re-applied, or a duplicate, it is deleted with its node; the complex ones are carried to the sense and pairing steps, which consider them first for correction, and the sweep judges what is left. The inner-being layer is required and specified, but it has not been run on any collection; the claims are not decided. The account, the claims and the narrative, is a complete draft assembled from readings made under earlier units, so it cannot yet be said to rest on the collections. The process control, with its escalation record, compliance check and session close, is operating. The current counts are held in the reports and not in this prose.

**What stands unsolved.** These gaps are recognised in the record and are not closed.
- No check of content exists before a stage closes. The structural checks of the application have passed while the content was wrong, and each content gap found so far was found by the researcher reading one case by hand.
- No independent control of completeness operates on the study's universe. The earlier controls, a comparison with the primary lexica, a lemma inventory and a candidate net, were each built and retired.
- The surfaces judged are those reached through the Strong's codes that the earlier cluster method allocated. A large share of the occurrences in the text lie on other codes and reach the study only as words that stand with member surfaces. Whether that boundary stays or widens is the researcher's to decide.
- The layered design has not been run through a stage on any collection, so it has not met the test at which an earlier reading technique failed, consistency at scale.
- The recorders of the layered reading were audited against the rules after the first run failed and not before it.

**What is not yet defined.** The programme states what it does not yet know, so that it is not mistaken for settled.
- The order in which the collections are taken is decided for each with its reason stated; it is not a rule.
- What a subgroup is for in stage 4 beyond carrying the senses on which the inner-being observations rest, and how the senses of a subgroup are fixed when the word readings are mixed: a judgement of reading, recorded with its reason.
- How the working of the inner being is depicted systematically and checked, and how a reading is kept consistent from one read to the next: the stage 4 steps are specified and have not been run, so what they leave is not yet known to be enough for this.
- The grain of the inner-being reading. A node is an occurrence of a word, while a working is a relation among occurrences; how one working across several nodes is one record is not stated. The unit of a batch of the inner-being reading, and how the nuances and variances of a working are handled when the same word works differently in different verses, are also not stated.
- The filter of the deeper reading by role: which verses and words go on to the deeper reading because the word has an inner-being role in them, and where in the claims phase that is applied. The roles of the nodes written by earlier methods are not all set (Chapter 4, the node), and setting them has been handed to the collection reading.
- The formulation of claims from the inner-being observations.
- How the chapters of the narrative follow the collections beyond the chapter on the inner being at work, which is built by collection. The researcher has called one chapter for each collection enormous and has said that the groupings are not yet known and should come from the claims; the rules that name the collection as the chapter would then be amended.
- How the per-cluster science reviews held as reference files are used in the claims reading; loading them into a reading was never built.
- The surfaces that were sorted wrongly, not yet judged or set aside: the step that records them, whether a surface rightly in a collection but set aside is read afterwards, and whether the surfaces that have no group set are in the collections or out of them.
- No check of content exists in the code; the reading is checked by Claude's own reading, recorded.

The programme's methods have changed materially over its life, as its record shows, and this section describes what operates now.
record.heading: Programme flow
record.author: claude_code

record.body:
The collection is read through the layered reading, run with `Collection-Build.ps1` (`GroupPull` and `GroupRecord` for the grouping, then `LayerOpen`, `LayerPull`, `LayerRecord` and `LayerCheck` for each subgroup in turn) over the steps and items of `cfg_setting layer.reading`. A step is opened only when the previous one is closed. The grouping is made first, from the WordNet tables, and is finished before any step of the loop opens; the loop then runs for one subgroup at a time on one set of data pulled once for the subgroup. The rows each step demands are the ledger `collection_layer_item`, derived from the data, each answered by an observation with its nodes or by a recorded none with its reason; a row is one unit of work and is updated at every event, not written at the end, so the table shows the processing as it goes, and a step closes only when every row is answered and validated. The stages and steps are described in Chapter 2, and the rules that govern them are configuration rows, delivered at the first use of the routine. The evidence on which a subgroup is read, its member occurrences, its senses and its pairings, is produced from the tables.

**The steps of the loop.** For each, the table gives what it asks, what it reads, how it is done and what it leaves. The observations of the first four are evidence; they say what the dictionary, the verses and the stored structure show and carry no inner-being role.

| Step | What it asks | What it reads | How it is done | What it leaves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The word step | In the verse of each occurrence, what is this word and how is it used here? | The subgroup's data: its surfaces with lettered Strong's codes, every verse they stand in (text and verse-lexical), the lexicon entries of each code, the old observations in scope. | One ledger row for each word (surface with its Strong's code), answered by the list of its observations. The old observations in scope are cleared: re-applied or corrected, or deleted with their nodes if still unmarked and not re-applied, or a duplicate; the complex ones are carried forward. | One observation for each distinct finding about the word, kind term (face where the sense departs), with a node of the role `lexical` for each occurrence it holds in. |
| Steps 1.1 and 1.2, the senses | What does each sense of the subgroup mean in context, as the Strong's code, the lexicon and the verse show it, and what do the codes of the sense say? | The word observations of the subgroup; the old observations carried forward, considered first for correction. | One row for the senses at 1.1 and one at 1.2, each answered by the list of senses; every word observation is carried by exactly one sense. | One observation for each sense (kind group) and one for its Strong's enrichment (kind enrichment), each with nodes on its occurrences and a traced node on each word observation it covers. |
| Step 2.1, the pairings | What stands with the subgroup in each verse: the words of other collections beside it, qualifiers and the words they reach, entities, the direction the text states, a double meaning? | The typed pairings from the subgroup's data and the WordNet pairings as a control. | One ledger row for each item (and, for pairings, each partner collection), answered by the list of its findings, and one for each surface with more than one code. | One observation for each distinct finding (kinds pairing, relation, face), with nodes for the subgroup's occurrences and the partner words in each verse it holds in, and traced nodes on the sense observations (and sometimes the word observations) it builds on. |
| The sweep | What is still unmarked and not applied? | The old observations in scope that are still of nature NULL. | Each is judged by content: marked evidence or inner being, or deleted with its node. | No observation of nature NULL is left in the subgroup's scope except one deferred to a named collection. |
| The evidence validation | Is the evidence layer of the subgroup complete? | The subgroup's observations. | A check of the tables; the content is read and recorded by Claude. | The gate before step 3.1. |

Every observation these steps leave states what the dictionary, the verses and the stored structure show, and carries no inner-being role. The inner-being layer (stage 4) follows, each step closed before the next opens. Its input is the evidence observations, the senses first; the behaviours are discovered from analysing those observations, with only occasional reading back into the verses, and every reading back is recorded with the verse and the reason. It sets observations and formulates no claim. Step 3.1, the elements of the subgroup, is the last step of the subgroup's loop: the findings (operation, polarity, object, enactment, party, circumstance, the role and dimension a variation gives, the chain, a flag) that its evidence shows, each resting on named observations by a traced node and carrying nodes with their roles; every evidence observation of the subgroup is rested on or declared not used with its reason. Step 3.2, the behaviours of the collection: the behaviours are discovered from the element observations of all the subgroups, each recorded as a discovery flag that names the behaviour and gathers its elements by traced nodes and makes no claim about it; every element is gathered or declared not gathered. Step 3.3, across collections: it reads all the observations whose nodes reference more than one collection and records one new observation for each unique match (a pairing of a word of this collection with a word of another collection that the nodes place together in a verse), tracing every observation the match comes from and holding the occurrences of both sides as nodes; it is the basis for a deeper analysis of what the pairing means, many matches will show nothing for the inner being, and that is known only later, so there is no minimum and no cap. It depends on the pairings and step 3.2 recording the collection on the nodes of both sides, and it opens only when that holds and the partner collections are complete, the collection status being checked and the researcher asked. The inner-being validation starts after the loop and completes after step 3.3, removing the inner-being observations that cannot be traced to evidence. The rules of the inner-being reading that the configuration holds (the observation items, the kinds of finding, the node roles, the method rules of the reading step and the nuance pointers) are its base; the interventions of the reading are prompted on every row.
